asks: what does Ambessa want to do
what's my job on this champ
say: Chain abilities with a dash after each one to trade and get out, or hold Repudiation for their big hit if they out-trade you.
more: Drakehound's Step gives a short dash, a stronger next attack and energy back whenever you move or attack during a cast. That one habit is both your trade pattern and your escape.
Early you win by short repeated trades. Later you look for Public Execution down a line, since it blinks you to the farthest champion in it and locks them down.
The trade-off is energy: spend it all going in and you have no dash left to leave.
check: Your energy bar, and whether their main damage ability has been used.
breaks: With no energy you have no dashes; back off and let it refill instead of walking in to attack.

asks: how do I trade on Ambessa
how do I win this lane
when do I go in on them
say: Sweep, dash out and repeat for short trades, or brace with Repudiation when they commit and slam back for the bigger hit.
more: Cunning Sweep hits harder on the blade edge, so space it at the edge and use the passive dash to step back out before they answer.
Repudiation shields you and deals more if it blocked champion or tower damage while you braced, so it rewards waiting for their attack rather than opening with it.
Short trades build a health lead that turns into a wave crash and a clean recall a couple of minutes later.
check: Whether their trading ability is ready, and how big the minion wave next to you is.
breaks: If they do not walk into you, do not force it through a big wave; farm with Lacerate and wait for the next opening.

asks: when am I strong on Ambessa
is six a spike for me
say: Level six gives you Public Execution, so look for a full all-in while it's up, or keep short trades if they're healthier.
more: Public Execution blinks to the target, suppresses them, then slams and stuns. That is enough lockdown to land everything else, which you did not have before six.
If you reach six first, the next trade is heavily in your favour. If they reach it first, give ground for that wave.
With a jungler nearby it is a guaranteed setup, so it is also worth holding for a gank.
check: Their health, their level, and whether they could simply walk under tower before you finish.
breaks: If they are level six first or far ahead in items, do not start the all-in; trade short and wait for your next item.

asks: what do I do in fights as Ambessa
who do I ult in a teamfight
where do I stand in a fight
say: Aim Public Execution down a line so it lands on a back-line carry, or stay and peel if their divers are on yours.
more: The ultimate goes to the farthest enemy champion in the line you choose, so angle matters more than timing. From the side it often skips their tank entirely.
After it lands you still have dashes from each ability to stick to them or leave.
Peeling is the right side of the trade when your carry is the reason you win later; you have a slow and a shield for that.
check: Who is actually farthest in the line you are aiming, and whether your team is close enough to follow.
breaks: If the farthest champion is a tank with their whole team around, do not go; fight the front line with your team instead.

asks: how do I play into ranged top
they keep poking me what do I do
how do I lane against a ranged champ
say: Into ranged tops, block poke with Repudiation and dash in when they miss a spell, or farm with Lacerate until your jungler comes.
more: Every ability gives you a dash, so two casts in a row cover a lot of ground once they have used the tool that keeps you off them.
Giving up a few minions to stay healthy is fine; you want to arrive at level six with enough health to threaten Public Execution.
check: Whether their escape or slow has just been used, and your own energy.
breaks: If they keep everything and just out-range you, stop trying to reach them; last-hit under tower and ask for a gank.

say: You're an all-in diver who heals by fighting, so only start fights you can finish, or cancel with Chilling Scream when it turns.
more: Blood Frenzy makes you chase the nearest enemy, champions first. Where you stand when you press it decides who you fight, so pick the spot before the button.
You have no natural health regeneration. Healing comes from the bleed, and it grows as your health drops, which is why low-health fights can still flip your way.
Chilling Scream ends the frenzy, heals and reduces damage. It is your only brake, so think twice before using it to start.
check: Who the nearest enemy will be when you press Blood Frenzy, and whether Chilling Scream is ready.
breaks: If the nearest target is a tank with their team behind, do not frenzy; wait for a pick or follow your own engage.

asks: how do I clear on Briar
do I full clear or gank on Briar
say: Full clear on Blood Frenzy and bleed healing toward your best lane, or gank at level three if a lane is set up.
more: Your attacks and abilities stack a bleed that heals you, so you stay healthy by hitting camps constantly. Standing still between camps costs you, since nothing regenerates.
A full clear is about level four with both crabs spawning at 2:55, so finishing on the side of your strongest lane gives you crab and a gank in one trip.
Briar leans toward ganking early because her stun and chase are strong, but she needs the health to commit.
check: Your health when the clear ends, and which lane has an enemy pushed up.
breaks: If you finish the clear low, take crab or reset first; a low Briar that frenzies into a lane often cannot get out.

asks: who do I gank on Briar
how do I gank with this champ
do I gank or keep farming
say: Gank the lane whose enemy is far up, leaping in with Head Rush for the stun, or countergank behind your laner if nobody's overextended.
more: Head Rush stuns and breaks armour, so the lane that follows up hardest on a stunned target is the one to visit. Blood Frenzy then keeps you on them.
Once frenzied you chase the nearest enemy, even toward their tower, so decide before you go in how far you are willing to follow.
A countergank suits you too: a fight already started means the nearest enemy is usually the one you want.
check: How far up the enemy laner is, and whether your laner has health and abilities to follow.
breaks: If the chase is heading under their tower, use Chilling Scream to stop and walk out rather than following in.

asks: what does my ult do for me
when am I strong on Briar
how do I use Certain Death
say: At six, Certain Death starts a fight from long range, so mark a carry who's alone, or hold it if nobody can follow.
more: Certain Death marks the first champion it hits as your prey, so anyone standing in front can take it instead. A clear line matters more than speed.
It turns a lane far from you into a gank without walking there, which is why your ganks get much harder to predict after six.
The cost is commitment: you end up deep on one target, so it should be a target that dies.
check: Whether anything stands between you and the target, and whether teammates are near enough to help.
breaks: If their whole team is around the target, keep it and fight normally; a marked tank in a crowd is how you die.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Briar
I keep dying first in fights
say: Go in after your front line so Blood Frenzy picks a good target, or flank with Certain Death onto a carry if they're busy.
more: Going second means their crowd control is already used and the nearest enemy is someone your team is already hitting.
Keep Chilling Scream for the moment you are focused: it heals, cuts damage taken and lets you choose a new target.
If you are ahead, the flank ends fights fast. If you are behind, going second with the team is much safer.
check: Which enemy is nearest before you frenzy, and whether their stuns have been used.
breaks: If nobody on your team can start, do not be the engage; wait for them to step onto your team and frenzy onto whoever dives.

say: Farm fast, stay hidden and win fights with a surprise Crowstorm, or look for Terrify picks from brush when it's down.
more: Terrify fears automatically when you damage someone with a spell while they cannot see you, so being unseen is your whole game. Fog and brush matter more than speed.
Early you are a farmer heading for level six. After that every lane and every objective has to respect a Crowstorm from somewhere dark.
The trade-off: if they have seen you, most of your threat is gone, so sometimes not showing is the play.
check: Whether the enemy can see where you are standing; the coach cannot see wards.
breaks: If they have vision of you, do not force the fight; back out, come from a different side, or just take camps.

asks: how do I clear on Fiddle
what's my first clear on Fiddlesticks
do I full clear or gank
where do I start on Fiddle
say: Full clear with Bountiful Harvest draining every monster near you and reach level four, or end crab side if a lane needs cover.
more: Bountiful Harvest drains health from all nearby enemies, so it damages a whole camp and heals you at once. That is why you clear healthy and fast.
A full clear is about level four, and both crabs spawn at 2:55, so finishing next to a river gives you the crab on the way out.
Fiddlesticks prefers farming early: ganks before Crowstorm are weak unless the lane brings its own lockdown.
check: Your health and mana at the end of the clear, and which river your last camp leaves you near.
breaks: If their jungler shows on the lane next to you, do not contest crab alone; give it and take your next camps.

asks: should I gank before six on Fiddle
my lane wants a gank what do I do
say: Before six, keep farming and only gank lanes with their own stun, or walk in from unseen brush so Terrify lands first.
more: Without Crowstorm your gank is a fear, a slow with a silence, and a drain. It works if the fear lands and your laner can lock them down after.
Every camp gets you closer to six, and six is when you actually take over. A failed gank delays that for both of you.
A countergank is different: sitting in brush behind your laner uses your kit well even before six.
check: Whether the lane has a ward covering your path, and whether your laner has crowd control ready.
breaks: If the enemy laner sees you coming, turn around early and go back to camps instead of walking down the lane.

asks: what do I do at six on Fiddle
I just hit six now what
say: Six is your real start: Crowstorm onto a pushed-up lane from out of sight, or save it for the next dragon fight.
more: Crowstorm damages everyone around you every second, and arriving unseen means Terrify fears them as it starts. Two enemies in a lane is the ideal first target.
Using it on a lane gets kills now. Holding it for dragon threatens the whole enemy team and can win the objective without a fight.
After it is used, go back to farming until it returns; you are much weaker without it.
check: Which lane has enemies past the middle, and whether you can reach a hidden spot beside them.
breaks: If nobody is pushed up, do not force it into a tower; farm and bring it to the next objective.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Fiddle
where do I stand in a fight
how do I teamfight on Fiddlesticks
say: Wait out of sight and Crowstorm onto their grouped back line, or stay by your carry and fear divers if you've been spotted.
more: You want to be the second thing that happens: your team starts, they clump up, and you arrive on top of them.
Reap silences the centre of its area, so after Crowstorm lands, put it on the champion most likely to escape or fight back.
If you are spotted, peeling with a point-and-click fear and a drain is still real value, just less of it.
check: Whether they can see you, and how tightly they are standing.
breaks: If they are spread out, do not ult one person in a crowd; use it to zone them off the objective instead.

asks: how do I use my scarecrow trinket
what do I do with effigies
where should I ward on Fiddle
say: Place effigies at the entrances to the next objective, or leave one in a lane brush to make that laner hesitate.
more: Your trinket is replaced by scarecrow effigies, so they are your warding tool. Put them where you would normally ward before an objective.
They look like you standing still, so one sitting in a brush can make a laner play scared even while you farm the other side.
check: Which objective is coming up next and which entrance the enemy is likely to use.
breaks: If you are behind and getting invaded, put effigies at your own jungle entrances instead of forward ones.

say: Stack your passive on minions, then fight with Bladesurge resets, or just farm until you have stacks and low minions nearby.
more: Hitting enemies with spells stacks attack speed, and at full stacks your attacks hit harder. You are a different champion stacked versus unstacked.
Bladesurge refreshes when it kills or hits a Marked target, and it heals you. A wave of low minions is your mobility, your sustain and your stacks.
So your fights depend on the wave: plenty of low minions means go, an empty lane means wait.
check: How many passive stacks you have, and which minions are low enough for Bladesurge to kill.
breaks: With no stacks and no low minions, do not start a fight; last-hit and wait for the next wave.

asks: how do I trade on Irelia
say: Dash through low minions to stack up, land Flawless Duet and Bladesurge the marked target, or back off if the wave's thin.
more: Flawless Duet stuns and Marks, and a Marked target refreshes Bladesurge. Landing it means two dashes on them and a stun to attack through.
Stacking on minions first matters: the same trade at full stacks does far more than one started cold.
Winning short trades this way sets up a crash and recall, and then your first item makes the next all-in much stronger.
check: Which minions Bladesurge will kill, and whether they still have the spell that stops your dash-in.
breaks: If Flawless Duet misses, do not commit; dash back to a low minion and reset the trade.

asks: when am I strong on Irelia
say: At six, Vanguard's Edge marks them for a free Bladesurge reset, so all-in with a wave behind you, or hold it for a gank.
more: Vanguard's Edge damages and Marks every champion it hits, so it guarantees a reset even if Flawless Duet misses.
Reaching six a wave earlier than them is the cleanest window. Check the levels before you go.
Because it Marks several champions, it is also strong when their jungler shows up: you get a reset on each.
check: Their level and health, your stacks, and how many minions each side has.
breaks: If they are six first or their wave is much bigger, keep the ultimate and farm; a failed all-in gives the lane away.

asks: how do I play into a bruiser
they out-trade me what do I do
how do I survive their burst
this lane is hard how do I play it
say: Into physical damage, charge Defiant Dance through their burst and trade back, or play for minion resets if they deal mostly magic.
more: Defiant Dance cuts physical damage while you charge it and hits harder the longer you hold. Timed on their big ability, it flips the trade.
Against magic damage it protects much less, so lean on Bladesurge healing off minions and dodge instead.
check: What kind of damage their main ability deals, and when they are about to use it.
breaks: If you charge it too early they just wait it out; hold it until they have actually committed.

asks: what do I do in fights as Irelia
how do I teamfight on Irelia
say: Open with Vanguard's Edge through several of them and dash between marks, or push a side lane if they have heavy lockdown.
more: Every Marked champion is a Bladesurge reset, so a wide ultimate lets you bounce through the fight while healing on each dash.
You are easy to stop once stunned in the middle, so going in after their crowd control is used keeps you alive.
In a side lane you have waves to reset on, which is where you are hardest to deal with one-on-one.
check: How many of them the ultimate can hit, and whether their stuns have been used.
breaks: If you are behind, do not go first; let your team start and come in from the side onto a carry.

say: You clean up: wait for a fight to start, then jump a low target for resets, or roam if your lane's stuck.
more: When a champion you damaged recently dies, your cooldowns drop dramatically. One kill gives you everything back for the next target.
So you want messy fights with low-health enemies, not a clean one-on-one against a full-health laner.
You have no mana or energy, so you can keep trading and shoving with Bouncing Blade all lane.
check: Who in the fight is low, and whether their stun or knock-up has been used.
breaks: If everyone is full health and holding crowd control, you are not the one to start; wait or go back to farming.

asks: how do I trade on Kat
how do I lane on Katarina
I can't farm in this lane
say: Bounce Bouncing Blade off minions to poke and last-hit, or Shunpo in for a short trade after their key spell is used.
more: Bouncing Blade jumps to nearby enemies, so throwing it at a minion beside them pokes without walking into range.
Shunpo puts you on top of them, which is a real commitment. Going in after they have used their main ability is when it is cheap.
Preparation gives a burst of move speed, so you can use it to walk out after a trade.
check: Whether their main damage or crowd-control spell was just used.
breaks: Into a lane that out-ranges you badly, give up some minions and farm with Bouncing Blade; your game starts with roams.

say: Shove the wave with Bouncing Blade and walk to a side-lane fight, or stay and farm if both side lanes are playing back.
more: You are stronger arriving at a fight already in progress than starting one, because a kill there resets you for the next target.
Pushing first means you lose little while away. Leaving a wave under your own tower hands your laner minions and tower damage.
A good roam before the first dragon often decides that objective too.
check: Where the side-lane waves are, and whether your own wave is pushed before you go.
breaks: If their laner follows you or the side lane backs off, turn around quickly instead of waiting in river.

asks: what do I do at six on Kat
how do I use Death Lotus
can I kill them at six
say: Death Lotus at six makes you a threat in any nearby fight, so look at river skirmishes, or all-in mid if they're low.
more: Death Lotus hits the three nearest enemy champions while you channel, so it does the most in a clumped fight, like a river skirmish.
It is a channel, so a stun or knock-up ends it early. Their crowd control being used is the real green light.
A kill during it brings your other abilities back, which is how one ultimate becomes two or three kills.
check: Whether the enemies nearby still have a stun, knock-up or silence available.
breaks: If they are holding crowd control for you, do not channel in the middle; poke and wait for it to be used.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Kat
I keep getting stunned in fights
how do I teamfight on Katarina
say: Stay out until their crowd control is used, then Shunpo in and channel Death Lotus, or pick off a straggler if they keep it.
more: Being late is correct for you. The fight starts, health bars drop, spells get used, and then you arrive for the resets.
Shunpo can target allies and minions as well as enemies, so you can use it to get out as well as in.
If you are ahead you can go a little earlier; if behind, only go for targets that are already low.
check: Which of their stuns are used and who is lowest.
breaks: If they are saving a stun for you, stay on the edge throwing Bouncing Blade and make them waste it first.

say: You win with short burst trades, so push for an early lead, or play for towers and dragons if the kills aren't there.
more: Each ability makes your next attack a double shot, so your damage comes in quick bursts: ability, attack, ability, attack.
Relentless Pursuit is a dash whose cooldown drops with those double shots, which lets you step in for a trade and back out.
That pattern is strongest while fights are short and small. An early lead matters more to you than to a late-game marksman.
check: Whether you are ahead of their marksman in minions and items.
breaks: If the lane is even or behind, stop forcing trades and just match farm; a dead Lucian gives the early game away.

asks: how do I trade on Lucian
say: Weave an attack between every ability for double shots, dashing in then out, or poke with Piercing Light through minions if they outrange you.
more: Casting two abilities back to back wastes a double shot. One attack between each cast gets the full damage out of the trade.
Piercing Light passes through its target, so aiming it at a minion in line with them pokes from a safer distance.
Ardent Blaze marks them and gives you move speed for attacking the mark, which helps you stick or leave.
check: Whether their engage or stun is ready before you dash forward.
breaks: If you dash in and their crowd control is still up, you have no way out; keep the dash and trade from range.

asks: when's my first spike on Lucian
do I push for level two
say: Push for level two first and dash in for a trade with two abilities, or hold the wave if their support has hard engage.
more: Two abilities means two double shots, and they may only have one ability yet. That short window is one of your best trades of the lane.
Winning it gives you health and wave control for the next few minutes, which is when junglers finish their first clears.
If their support can lock you down, pushing up for it is the risk; an even wave is safer.
check: Which side hits the minions faster, and what their support can do at level one.
breaks: If they will reach level two first, back off before it happens and give the push.

asks: how do I play with my support
when do I fight with my support
how do I use my passive with my support
what does my support do for me
say: Fight the moment your support shields you or locks someone down for bonus damage, or trade alone with ability-attack combos if they've roamed.
more: When an ally heals or shields you, or a nearby enemy champion is immobilized, your next two attacks deal bonus magic damage.
So a shield from an enchanter or a stun from an engage support is your cue to attack, not just protection.
Timing your dash-in with it is what turns a normal trade into a kill threat.
check: What your support's abilities do, and whether they are ready and in range.
breaks: If your support is away or out of mana, play the lane like a one-on-two: last-hit and keep the dash.

asks: how do I play mid game on Lucian
what do I do after lane
say: Turn your lead into towers and dragons while fights are small, or play behind your front line if it's gone even.
more: Your burst pattern is at its best in skirmishes of two or three. Use that time to take the things that last: towers and dragons.
Four elemental dragons give soul, so early dragons you help take keep paying later, when longer-range carries catch up.
If it is even, you are a normal marksman: hit the nearest target and keep the dash for safety.
check: The gold and item gap between you and their carry, and which objective is next.
breaks: If their carry out-ranges you and is ahead, do not walk up to duel; fight only with your team in front.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Lucian
where do I stand in fights
say: Hit whoever's closest and keep Relentless Pursuit to dodge their engage, or dash forward with The Culling once their threats are spent.
more: Dashing forward first leaves you with nothing when their diver arrives. Keeping it is what keeps you alive late.
The Culling is a long stream of shots in one direction, best on a slowed or locked-down target or down a narrow path.
Once their engage is used, you can play forward freely and your burst finishes people.
check: Whether their engage and assassin abilities have been used.
breaks: If an assassin is waiting for you, stay next to your support and do not use the dash to attack.

say: Stack Siphoning Strike on every minion you safely can and run them down later, or give up minions to stay healthy early.
more: Siphoning Strike gets permanently stronger each time it kills its target. Your whole game is how many of those you collect.
Early you are weak and that is fine. Lifesteal from your passive keeps you in lane while you last-hit.
Later, Wither makes one enemy slow in both movement and attacks, and a stacked Siphoning Strike breaks towers and people.
check: Your Siphoning Strike stack count against the game time; the coach cannot see stacks.
breaks: If chasing a stack means taking a bad trade, skip it; a death costs far more stacks than one minion.

asks: how do I lane on Nasus
where do I want the wave
say: Let the wave come to your side and last-hit with Siphoning Strike, or give a few minions rather than trade with a bully.
more: A wave near your tower is safe from ganks and makes them walk far up to bother you, which is exactly where your jungler wants them.
Only last-hitting keeps it there. Using Spirit Fire on the wave pushes it and takes last hits away from Siphoning Strike.
This is slow on purpose: every minute you survive while stacking moves the lane toward you.
check: Which way the wave is pushing, and your health and mana.
breaks: If they freeze the wave on their side, do not walk up for it; ask for jungle help or wait for the next push.

asks: when can I fight on Nasus
say: At six, Fury of the Sands lets you fight back, so trade when they overstep, or keep stacking if they're well ahead.
more: Fury of the Sands is your first real fighting tool: with Wither slowing their attacks, a bully who dives you can lose the trade.
Your bigger spike is stacks plus your first completed item, so even with the ultimate the default is still to farm.
Use it to survive ganks and dives too. Staying alive protects the stacks you would have missed while dead.
check: Their items compared with yours, and how many stacks you have.
breaks: If they are far ahead, the ultimate only keeps you alive; use it to escape, not to chase.

asks: do I split or group on Nasus
what do I do mid game
should I stay in side lane
say: Push a side lane and keep stacking so they must send two, or join your team if an objective is about to spawn.
more: Side waves are stacks, and a stacked Siphoning Strike takes towers fast. One person usually cannot stop you, so they send two.
When two come to you, your team has an extra player for dragon or baron. That is the trade you are offering.
Push the lane on the far side from the next objective so the walk for them is long.
check: Where their team is on the map, and whether your side lane has vision around it.
breaks: If three or more are missing and you are past the river, back off; coming to you should cost them an objective, not give them a kill.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Nasus
do I go for their carry
how do I teamfight on Nasus
say: Wither their fastest attacker and walk at the carries, or stay back and Wither whoever dives if your own carry wins the game.
more: Wither slows both movement and attack speed over time, so on an attack-based carry it removes most of their damage for the fight.
Spirit Fire reduces the armour of anyone standing on it. Put it where the fight is happening so your whole team benefits.
You have no dash, so you get kited. Wither on the person you are chasing is how you actually reach them.
check: Which enemy deals damage with attacks, and who is the bigger threat to your carry.
breaks: If you cannot reach the back line, stop walking at it; hit the nearest target and protect your own.

asks: how do I play into ranged top on Nasus
they poke me off every minion
I can't stack in this lane
how do I survive this lane
say: Into ranged tops, last-hit with Spirit Fire from range and heal with lifesteal, or ask for a gank when they push to your tower.
more: Spirit Fire reaches minions you cannot walk up to. You lose the stack on those, but you keep the gold and experience.
Their constant pushing puts them far from their tower, which makes this one of the easier lanes for your jungler to gank.
The goal is to reach six and your first item without dying, not to win the lane.
check: Your mana, since Spirit Fire farming drains it, and how far up they are standing.
breaks: If you are being poked under tower with low health, recall early; losing one wave beats dying to a dive.

say: Bully the melee laner with ranged attacks and Harrier marks, then roam with your ultimate, or split push if roams aren't open.
more: You are a ranged champion in a mostly melee lane, and Harrier marks make single attacks hurt. The early lane is where you build a lead.
Behind Enemy Lines lets you fly around the map at great speed, so after six that lead can be spent in other lanes.
The trade-off is that you are fragile: if a fight reaches you, Vault is your only way out.
check: Whether the enemy top laner has a way to close the distance onto you.
breaks: If you fall behind, stop roaming into fights; push side waves and take what is free.

asks: how do I trade on Quinn
how do I bully this lane
say: Attack when Harrier marks them for the bonus hit, and Vault away when they jump you, or hold Vault if you're pushed up.
more: Valor marks enemies now and then, and your first attack on a marked target deals bonus damage and triggers Heightened Senses speed.
Vault dashes to them and slows them, and that slow is what lets you walk away from a diver. Using it to attack leaves you without that.
Blinding Assault hinders their vision, which shuts down champions who need to see you to hit back.
check: Whether Vault is ready, and how far the wave has pushed you up the lane.
breaks: If you are past the middle with Vault used, step back to your side until it returns.

asks: what do I do at six on Quinn
should I roam with my ult
how do I use Behind Enemy Lines
say: At six, shove the wave and fly mid for a gank with Behind Enemy Lines, or use it to get back to lane fast.
more: The speed means you can leave lane, gank and return while losing very little, as long as your wave was pushed first.
Ending the flight casts Skystrike, which damages nearby enemies and marks champions with Harrier, so you arrive with a marked target.
Using it only to return to lane is lower value but keeps constant pressure on a melee laner.
check: Where the mid wave is, and whether their mid laner is past the halfway point.
breaks: If your own wave is not pushed, do not go; you lose minions and tower health for a maybe.

asks: do I split or group on Quinn
what do I do mid game
where do I go after lane
say: Push a far side lane and fly out when they collapse, or fly to your team first if a dragon fight is starting.
more: Your speed lets you push deeper than most champions safely, and then still arrive at a fight on the other side of the map.
Making one or two of them answer you gives your team numbers elsewhere. Showing in the side lane just before an objective is the timing.
You duel most champions that cannot reach you, but lose to ones that can.
check: How many enemies are visible, and who they are sending to stop you.
breaks: If the one coming to answer you can jump onto you, do not duel; leave and push the next wave.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Quinn
where do I stand in fights
say: Stay on the edge hitting marked targets and use Blinding Assault on their main attacker, or flank late onto a carry who's alone.
more: Blinding Assault hinders the vision of the enemy it marks, so on a champion that attacks to deal damage it takes them out of the fight briefly.
You are an extra marksman in a normal fight. The flank works because you move fast enough to arrive after their abilities are used.
Either way, Vault is for getting away, so do not open with it.
check: Who their biggest attack-based threat is, and whether a carry is standing apart from the group.
breaks: If the flank path has no vision, stay with your team; a caught Quinn dies before the fight starts.

asks: how do I not get ganked on Quinn
how do I check for their jungler
what do I do with Heightened Senses
say: Use Heightened Senses to check river before you push past halfway, or keep the wave on your side while it's down.
more: Activating Heightened Senses has Valor reveal a large area nearby. It is a free look at the river or the brush you were about to walk past.
You push a lot as a ranged laner, so you are the lane junglers want to visit. Checking first is what lets you keep bullying.
check: Whether Heightened Senses is ready, and where the wave is.
breaks: If the reveal shows nothing but their jungler has not been seen anywhere, still play near your side until they show.

say: Stay behind your team, poke and shield, and save Encore for a grouped fight, or protect one fed carry if that's how you win.
more: Every third basic spell casts twice, so planning which spell lands third is most of your skill: a double poke, a double shield or a double slow.
You get better the more champions are around you: Surround Sound helps every nearby ally and Encore extends through each champion it touches.
Small skirmishes far from your team are where you are weakest.
check: Which spell will be your third cast, and how many allies are near you.
breaks: If you are caught alone, do not fight; slow with Beat Drop and walk back to your team.

asks: how do I trade on Seraphine
how do I lane on Sera
what do I do with the double cast
say: Line up the doubled third spell as High Note for poke, or as Surround Sound when they're about to trade into you.
more: A doubled High Note is your best poke. A doubled Beat Drop on an already slowed target holds them in place much longer.
Surround Sound heals as well if you are already shielded, so the doubled cast gives both the shield and the heal.
Casting near an ally also gives your next attack extra damage and range, so add an attack after spells.
check: Your spell count toward the third cast, and your mana.
breaks: If mana is low, stop poking and keep it for Surround Sound; a shield in the next fight matters more.

asks: what do I do at six on Seraphine
say: At six, Encore through both of them starts a winning fight, so call your jungler, or hold it to stop their engage.
more: Encore charms everyone it hits, so both enemy laners caught together is a long window for your marksman and jungler to attack freely.
Used second, it answers their all-in: they jump on you, you charm them mid-dive, and the fight flips.
Which one is right depends on who starts fights in your lane.
check: Whether both enemies are lined up, and whether your jungler is near.
breaks: If they have a stronger engage than you, do not start with it; keep it for when they come in.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Seraphine
how do I teamfight on Sera
say: Fire Encore through your own front line into theirs for the extra reach, or hold it to charm whoever dives your carry.
more: Encore refreshes its range with every champion it hits, allies included, so sending it through your team lets it reach much further than expected.
Stand where Surround Sound covers as many allies as possible. A doubled one on a grouped team is a huge swing.
Around a dragon or baron pit, where everyone is packed tight, is where it does the most.
check: How tightly both teams are grouped, and where their divers are.
breaks: If their team is spread wide, do not chase a big ultimate; use it on the one diver who matters.

asks: how do we win from here
say: You're best in grouped fights, so walk with your team to each dragon, or clear side waves from range if they're splitting.
more: Everything you have hits or helps several champions at once, so five-on-five fights around an objective suit you far more than small skirmishes.
Dragon respawns five minutes after a kill, so grouping a little before each one is a simple plan to repeat.
If your team wants to split, your job becomes clearing waves safely so towers hold.
check: When the next dragon is due, and whether your team is actually grouping.
breaks: If your team keeps fighting spread out, stay next to your strongest carry and play only for them.

say: Control lane with Dark Sphere poke and threaten a burst with all your spheres, or play safe and scale if you're being camped.
more: Dark Spheres stay on the ground after they land. Scatter the Weak pushes them and stuns whoever they hit, and Unleashed Power throws all of them at one champion.
So spheres on the ground are both your stun and your kill damage. More spheres out means more threat.
You have no dash, so your safety is distance and keeping the stun ready.
check: How many spheres are on the ground, and whether you still have Scatter the Weak.
breaks: If their jungler keeps coming mid, stop stepping up to poke; farm with spheres from your side.

asks: how do I trade on Syndra
should I use my stun to trade
say: Poke with Dark Sphere when they step up to last-hit, or keep Scatter the Weak for self-defence if they can jump you.
more: They have to stand still for a moment to last-hit. That is the easy time to land a sphere.
Force of Will can throw a sphere or a minion and slows whoever it hits, which makes the next sphere easier.
Using the stun to trade is strong but leaves you open, so against a champion with a gap closer it is better held.
check: Whether their gap closer is ready, and your mana.
breaks: If you miss the stun and they can reach you, walk back immediately rather than finishing the trade.

asks: what do I do at six on Syndra
can I kill them at six
how do I use my ult
say: At six, stun with a sphere then Unleashed Power to finish a weakened target, or keep poking until they're low enough.
more: Unleashed Power uses every Dark Sphere you have, so throw one or two down first and the ultimate hits harder.
It is a point-and-click finish, so the question is only whether the damage is enough. Poke first, then commit.
A kill at six usually gives you the wave and a free trip to the river fight after.
check: Their health, how many spheres are out, and whether they have a shield or heal available.
breaks: If they are still healthy, do not spend it; the threat of it keeps them off the wave anyway.

say: Hitting champions collects Splinters that upgrade your spells, so keep poking, or farm safely and take them from levels if it's risky.
more: Splinters of Wrath come from gaining levels and from damaging enemies. They upgrade abilities, for example an extra Dark Sphere charge and bonus true damage on Force of Will.
So steady poke in lane is not just chip damage; it makes you stronger for the rest of the game.
Levels give them too, so a safe lane still scales, just more slowly.
check: Your Splinter count, which the coach cannot see.
breaks: If poking means standing where their jungler can reach you, take the slow route and collect from levels.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Syndra
who do I stun in a fight
say: Stand back, stun whoever walks up with Scatter the Weak and burst the first carry in range, or save the stun for their diver.
more: Scatter the Weak can stun several champions if spheres are spread in front of you, which stops an engage before it starts.
Unleashed Power on a carry removes them at the start. On a tank it mostly wastes your biggest spell.
Against assassins or divers, holding the stun for yourself keeps you alive to cast a second round.
check: Who can reach you, and which of their carries is in range.
breaks: If only their tank is in range, do not ult it; poke with spheres and wait for a better target.

say: Poke from range with charged Piercing Arrows before fights, or attack up close stacking Blight and popping it, depending on your items.
more: Piercing Arrow gains range and damage the longer you charge it. That makes you a poke champion who softens people before a fight.
Attacks apply Blight and your other abilities detonate it for damage based on their maximum health. That is your steady damage into tougher targets.
Chain of Corruption is real lockdown, so you can start fights as well as follow them.
check: Which way your items lean, and whether their team is tanky or fragile.
breaks: If nobody on your team can protect you, lean on poke from range instead of standing in attack range.

asks: how do I trade on Varus
when do I use Piercing Arrow
say: Stack Blight with a few attacks then pop it with Piercing Arrow, or just poke with charged arrows if their engage is scary.
more: Blight detonation is where your trade damage comes from, so attack first and cast second rather than opening with the arrow.
Hail of Arrows slows and cuts their healing and regeneration, so it also pops Blight and makes their sustain worse.
Charged arrows from far away cost you nothing in return damage, which is the safe way to play a lane you cannot walk up in.
check: How many Blight stacks are on them, and whether their engage is ready.
breaks: If walking up to attack gets you engaged on, stay back and poke only.

asks: what do I do at six on Varus
how do I use my ult
say: At six, Chain of Corruption locks one down and can spread, so all-in or call a gank, or keep it for their dive.
more: It immobilizes the first champion hit and then spreads to nearby champions, so two laners standing together can both be caught.
Landing it makes a jungle gank almost certain to work, so tell your jungler when it is ready.
Held back, it stops whoever jumps on you and often turns their all-in into your kill.
check: Whether the two of them are standing close together, and where your jungler is.
breaks: If their lane has stronger engage than yours, do not open with it; use it on whoever comes in.

asks: how do I deal with their tank
they heal too much what do I do
I can't kill their front line
how do I play into tanks on Varus
say: Into tanks, stack Blight and detonate it since it scales with their health, or lead with Hail of Arrows on big healers.
more: Blight detonation deals damage based on the target's maximum health, so the more health they have, the more it hurts.
Hail of Arrows leaves ground that slows and reduces self-healing and regeneration. Put it under the champion that heals through fights.
This makes you a good front-line killer, which is useful when you cannot reach their back line.
check: Who on their team has the most health, and who is healing the most.
breaks: If a tank is on top of you, do not stand and stack; move back first and stack while walking away.

when: a dragon or baron is about a minute from spawning
asks: what do I do before dragon
how do I set up baron on Varus
should I poke before the fight
how do we get this objective
say: Get there early and poke with charged Piercing Arrows so they arrive low, or trade for something across the map if you're late.
more: A team that walks to an objective at half health cannot contest it. Your poke can win the fight before it starts.
Being first also means you choose where to stand. Arriving second, you would be poking into a team already set up.
If you are late, taking a tower or camps on the other side is better than walking into their setup.
check: Whether your team is already there, and where the enemy is coming from.
breaks: If they have hard engage and can reach you while you charge, poke from behind your front line or not at all.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Varus
who do I hit in fights
say: Poke before the fight, then immobilize their first diver with Chain of Corruption, or open with it if you catch someone.
more: Late game one catch often decides it, and your ultimate spreading through a clumped team is one of the better ways to start.
If their divers are the danger, holding it keeps you alive, and a kill or assist then boosts your damage through your passive.
After it is used, hit the nearest target and keep stacking Blight.
check: Who can dive you, and whether an enemy is out of position.
breaks: If you miss the ultimate, back up and play at maximum range until it returns.

asks: how do I play Xin Zhao
say: You're strong early, so gank and skirmish for a lead before items, or become the front-line peeler if the game goes long.
more: Your kit is simple and front-loaded: a charge, a slow, a knock-up on the third hit and a heal on every third attack.
That wins small early fights. Later, enemies have the items to burst or kite you, so the lead you build early is what you play on.
If you do not get it, you still have a knock-up and a slow to protect your carry.
check: Whether your lanes can follow up on your ganks.
breaks: If you are behind, stop looking for duels; stay with your team and play to peel.

asks: how do I clear on Xin Zhao
where do I start on Xin
do I full clear or gank
say: Start away from the lane you want and gank it at level three, or full clear to level four if lanes are pushing.
more: Every third attack heals you, and Audacious Charge gives attack speed, so you clear healthy enough to gank straight afterwards.
Level three gives you all three basic abilities. Arriving in a lane then, before they expect anyone, is your signature play.
Xin Zhao leans toward ganking early; a full clear is the fallback when no lane is gankable.
check: Which lane has an enemy pushed up as you finish your third camp.
breaks: If the gank is not there, do not wait in a brush; go back and finish your camps before crab at 2:55.

asks: how do I gank on Xin
say: Slow them with Wind Becomes Lightning first so Audacious Charge reaches from further, or just charge and knock up if you're close.
more: Wind Becomes Lightning marks them as Challenged, and Audacious Charge has longer range onto Challenged targets. That is how you gank from outside normal reach.
Then Three Talon Strike knocks up on the third attack, so your laner has a slow and a knock-up to follow.
Pick the lane with damage ready; your lockdown is short, so someone has to finish it.
check: How far up the enemy is, and whether your laner has health and abilities.
breaks: If you miss Wind Becomes Lightning and they are far away, do not charge anyway; walk off and keep your path.

asks: do I go into their jungle
say: Step into their jungle for a duel when the lanes beside you can move first, or mirror their path and countergank instead.
more: A charge, a knock-up and a third-hit heal make you hard to beat in an early one-on-one, but only if nobody else arrives.
Lanes that can leave first decide it. If theirs get there first, your duel becomes a two-on-one.
Counterganking uses the same strength with less risk: you fight their jungler with your laner beside you.
check: Whether the lanes next to that jungle are pushed toward the enemy, and your own health.
breaks: If their lanes have the push, do not go in; take your own camps and wait for them to come to you.

asks: when am I strong on Xin
say: Level three gives you slow, charge and knock-up together, so gank now, or wait for level four if both lanes are pushed up.
more: With all three basic abilities you already have your full gank. Most junglers are still finishing camps at that point.
An early kill here matters twice: your laner gets ahead, and you get the gold while your kit is at its strongest.
At six, Crescent Guard challenges whoever you damaged recently, which adds to your duels.
check: Whether a lane is gankable right now, and your health after three camps.
breaks: If your own laners are the ones pushed up, a gank will not work; finish the clear and look after crab.

asks: what do I do in teamfights as Xin
how do I teamfight on Xin Zhao
say: Charge their carry if your team is right behind you, or stand by your own carry and knock up whoever dives.
more: Charging in alone late usually means dying before the knock-up lands. It works when your team is close enough to hit the same target.
Peeling uses the same buttons: slow the diver with Wind Becomes Lightning, knock them up with Three Talon Strike.
Which is right depends on who is stronger: go in if you are ahead, protect if their divers are.
check: How close your team is, and which side has the stronger carry.
breaks: If your team is not following, do not go; stay in front of your carry and fight whoever comes to you.
